title: The isolated sixth gelsolin repeat and headpiece domain of villin bundle F-actin in the presence of calcium and are linked by a 40-residue unstructured sequence.
experiment: 15N R1, R2 and heteronuclear {1H-15N}-NOE at 750 MHz (FAST-Modelfree Lipari-Szabo S2 analysis)
buffer: 1.1 mM D6-HP, 10% 2H2O, 5 mM CaCl2, 10 mM d10-DTT, 0.01% NaN3, 20 mM d18-PIPES
construct_or_mutation: D6-HP (C-terminal 208 residues of chicken villin: D6 domain 1-105, linker 105-145, headpiece HP 145-206; construct numbering)
other_conditions: 仅图示 (per-residue R1, R2, {1H-15N}-NOE and S2 profiles for 144 of 176 assigned amides plotted in Fig. 4 and sequence in Fig. 5; deposited in BMRB 15097); 32 assigned resonances excluded due to low intensity or overlap; R1 delays 100-2000 msec, R2 delays 10-250 ms, NOE presaturation 2.5 sec; F84 in D6 has {1H-15N}-NOE ratio well below 0.6, low R2, and was marked 'unassigned' by FAST-Modelfree; pH adjusted without correction for 2H2O
residues_author: F84 (in D6 domain); linker 104-144 / 105-145 (disordered); structured domains 1-105 (D6) and 145-206 (HP)
related_structures: BMRB 15097 (D6-HP assignments and relaxation data); BMRB 4428 (isolated headpiece HP67); gelsolin G6 crystal structures (refs. 21, 22) and villin HP67 structures (refs. 16, 17), PDB IDs not printed in text
author_claim: 15N R1, R2, heteronuclear {1H-15N}-NOE, and Lipari-Szabo S2 order parameters show that Ca2+-bound D6-HP comprises two structured domains—D6 (positions 1-105) and HP (145-206)—connected by an unstructured, highly flexible ~40-residue linker (105-145 / 104-144), while within D6 residue Phe84 appears locally unstructured (low R2 and {1H-15N}-NOE well below 0.6).
anchor: The 15N backbone relaxation rates R1 and R2 as well as the {1H-15N}-NOE (Figure 4 A,B,C) indicate three distinct structural entities within D6-HP, namely two structured regions, positions 1-105 and 145-206, and a disordered sequence in between.
locator: p. 6 Results, p. 8-9 Discussion, and Figure 4 (p. 16, 仅图示 for full 144-residue profiles); conditions: p. 4-5 Materials and methods (NMR data collection and processing; NMR relaxation measurements and order parameter computations)
caveat_note: The NMR sample in this paper (deposited in BMRB 15097 at 750 MHz, 25 °C = 298.15 K) is the 208-residue two-domain chicken villin fragment D6-HP (D6 + 40-residue linker + HP), whereas the manifest card specifies 'Villin-1 D6 domain' with sequence_length = 107, sheet_temperature_K = 298.0, sheet_field_MHz = 750, and blank BMRB fields (RelaxDB likely cropped residues 1-107 from BMRB 15097). Linker boundaries are written both as 105-145 (pp. 6, 9) and 104-144 (p. 6); p. 9 line 587 cites 'Figure 4C' for low R2 of Phe84 (R2 is Fig. 4B, NOE is Fig. 4C).

title: The isolated sixth gelsolin repeat and headpiece domain of villin bundle F-actin in the presence of calcium and are linked by a 40-residue unstructured sequence.
experiment: 2D 15N HSQC and 3D triple-resonance assignment spectra at 600, 750 and 800 MHz
buffer: 1.1 mM D6-HP, 10% 2H2O, 5 mM CaCl2, 10 mM d10-DTT, 0.01% NaN3, 20 mM d18-PIPES
ligand_or_partner: 5 mM CaCl2 (Ca2+-saturated; unchanged from 5 to 50 mM Ca2+)
construct_or_mutation: D6-HP (C-terminal 208 residues of chicken villin: D6 domain 1-105, linker 105-145, headpiece HP 145-206; construct numbering)
other_conditions: regime (authors): intermediate structural exchange on the NMR time scale; 仅图示 (unassigned lowercase positions mapped on full sequence in Fig. 5); 17 total unassigned residues in D6-HP: 4 N-terminal, 2 C-terminal, and 11 internal residues (including 3 prolines) within D6 positions 60-85 flanked by weak or missing 15N-HSQC peaks
residues_author: A60, Q61, E62, P68-D72, E85 (within 11 unassigned internal D6 positions 60-85)
related_structures: BMRB 15097 (D6-HP); BMRB 4428 (HP67); gelsolin G6 crystal structure (ref. 22), PDB ID not printed in text
author_claim: Eleven internal residues within positions 60-85 of the D6 domain lack backbone assignments and are flanked by weak or missing 15N-HSQC resonances; Pro68-Asp72 and Glu85 correspond to solvent-exposed loops in gelsolin G6 and are proposed to undergo intermediate structural exchange on the NMR timescale.
anchor: Because this region corresponds to the solvent-exposed loop in the crystal structure of the G6 domain of gelsolin (22), we propose that these residues are involved in intermediate structural exchange which weakens their NMR resonances.
locator: p. 5-6 Results, p. 8-9 Discussion, and Figure 5 (p. 17, 仅图示 for full unassigned sequence map); conditions: p. 4 Materials and methods (NMR data collection and processing)
caveat_note: For the second longest unassigned stretch Ala60-Gln61-Glu62 (corresponding to an internal region of the longest helix in gelsolin G6), the authors explicitly state that why these residues could not be assigned remains unclear. Measured on the 208-residue D6-HP construct (BMRB 15097) rather than an isolated 107-residue D6 construct.

title: The isolated sixth gelsolin repeat and headpiece domain of villin bundle F-actin in the presence of calcium and are linked by a 40-residue unstructured sequence.
experiment: 2D 15N HSQC comparison of Ca2+-free (apo) vs 5 mM Ca2+ D6-HP
buffer: Ca2+-free D6-HP sample (compared against 1.1 mM D6-HP, 10% 2H2O, 5 mM CaCl2, 10 mM d10-DTT, 0.01% NaN3, 20 mM d18-PIPES pH 7.0; exact Ca2+-free NMR salt/buffer composition not listed separately)
ligand_or_partner: none (apo / Ca2+-free vs 5 mM Ca2+ reference)
construct_or_mutation: D6-HP (C-terminal 208 residues of chicken villin: D6 domain 1-105, linker 105-145, headpiece HP 145-206; construct numbering)
other_conditions: Without >1 mM Ca2+, D6-HP aggregates within hours into oligomeric gel-filtration peaks II and III (Fig. 2A) and shows fewer 15N-HSQC peaks than expected plus broad random-coil peaks; 96 amides assigned in Ca2+-free HSQC (33 in D6, 27 in linker, 36 in HP); positions 81-105 of D6, linker, and HP (including D166) are Ca2+-insensitive
residues_author: 1-80 (Ca2+-sensitive N-terminal region of D6; proposed Ca2+-site N29, D30, E52 = chicken villin N647, D648, E670)
related_structures: BMRB 15097 (Ca2+-bound D6-HP); gelsolin Ca2+-free and Ca2+-bound crystal structures (refs. 21, 22), PDB IDs not printed in text
author_claim: In the absence of calcium, one quarter of D6 backbone amide resonances (localized to the first 80 residues of D6) disappear or shift significantly and broad random-coil peaks appear, indicating unfolding/destabilization of residues 1-80 of D6 (accompanied by slow aggregation over hours), whereas D6 residues 81-105, the linker, and HP remain unaffected.
anchor: Without calcium, one quarter of all the D6 backbone amide resonances either disappear or have significant changes in their chemical shift values.
locator: p. 5 Results (Calcium is required for stability...) and p. 7 Results (Calcium binds to the D6 domain); conditions: p. 4-5 Materials and methods and p. 7 Results
caveat_note: Peak disappearance and broad random-coil signals in Ca2+-free D6-HP reflect Ca2+-depletion unfolding/destabilization of D6 residues 1-80 confounded by time-dependent oligomerization/aggregation over hours when [Ca2+] < 1 mM (Fig. 2A; authors state 'a significant fraction of unfolded structure and/or protein aggregation'). Also differs from the Ca2+-bound BMRB 15097 / RelaxDB VILD6 condition (5 mM CaCl2) and uses the 208-residue D6-HP construct.
